subtitle: Your agents, out loud
description:
Claude Code runs in a VM, a container or a server with no speaker. Ralk is the tab on the machine in front of you: a chime when the build finishes, Olivia's voice when something needs you, a browser notification when you're in another window.

Connect Claude, Claude Code or ChatGPT once. From then on Claude can tell you a task is done, that it needs your approval, that something broke, or ask a question: each kind has its own sound, and a spoken line follows a few seconds later. Every device you have open plays it; the card says which one heard it.

The 52 sounds are made from code in your browser, nothing to download, and you pick which one goes with each kind. The voice is Inworld TTS on fal.ai, Olivia by default, any of its voices with a sample; a line said before plays again at once and costs nothing.

It feels like an app: a bar that stays put, one panel that scrolls, a tab bar on your phone, light and dark, and sounds you can try before you sign in.
whatsNew: Ralk opens like an app now: the page draws at once from what your browser kept, and every file comes from the app itself, not the network. ⌘K goes to a tab or opens Connect via MCP…, the sidebar hides with one click, and each tab keeps its place while you're on another. A long path in a notification wraps at its slashes.
